en: Hello, we need a repair visit on the {system} system on {field}. Please tell us your first free day and a price. The lines must be flushed by {flush_date}.
Hello, the pump at {name} ({pump_kw} kW) is due for service on {pump_service}. Please book a visit and send a price for oil, seals and a motor check.
Hello, we need the soil test results for {field} before we finish the fertiliser plan. The last test was on {soil_test_on}. Please send them as soon as you can.
Hello, the leaves on {field} ({crop}) look pale and may show a nutrient deficiency. The plan is {n_ha} kg of nitrogen per ha and we have applied {n_done} so far. Can you visit this week?
Hello, we plan {n_ha} kg of nitrogen per hectare for {field} ({crop}). Do you advise two or three doses? We have applied {n_done} kg per ha so far.
Hello {operator}, we spread {kind} on {field} on {date}: {tonnes} tonnes, {n_ha} kg of nitrogen per hectare. Please keep clear of streams, wells and the boundary strip.
Hello {neighbour}, we plan to take our turn from {name} this week. Please tell us when you take yours so that we do not both open the gate.
Hello, the pump at {source} used {kwh} kWh in the week of {week} and cost {cost}, which is {cost_m3} per m3 and above our limit. Please check the pump, the pressure and the start time.
Hello {keeper}, please bring the delivery notes and the receipts for {item} to the office today so that the invoice can be checked and paid.
Hello {keeper}, the count of {item} shows {counted} {unit} but the sheet says {balance}. The difference is {diff}. Please recount and tell me what happened.
Field: {col:fertplan.field}. Crop: {col:fertplan.crop}. Area: {col:fertplan.area} hectares. Prepared by {col:fertplan.prepared_by}.

We plan {col:fertplan.n_ha} kg of nitrogen, {col:fertplan.p_ha} kg of P2O5 and {col:fertplan.k_ha} kg of K2O for each hectare. For the whole field this is {col:fertplan.n_total} kg of nitrogen, {col:fertplan.p_total} kg of P2O5 and {col:fertplan.k_total} kg of K2O. The plan follows the soil test of {col:fertplan.soil_test_on}.

So far fertiliser and manure have put on {col:fertplan.n_done} kg of nitrogen per hectare, which is {col:fertplan.n_share} of the plan. The plan check shows: {col:fertplan.state}. The nitrogen balance against what the crop removes is {col:fertplan.n_bal} kg per hectare.
The supervisor spreads only what this plan allows and writes every application in the application record. Any change of rate is agreed with the crop manager first.
We order {col:orders.qty_ordered} {col:orders.unit} of {col:orders.item} at {col:orders.price} per {col:orders.unit}. The order value is {col:orders.value}.

Please deliver on {col:orders.promised}. Send the delivery note with the batch or lot number and the weight, and tell us before the delivery if you cannot keep the date. The status of the order is {col:orders.status}.
We check every delivery against this order. A short or late delivery will be recorded in your supplier performance.
Field: {col:costha.field}. Crop: {col:costha.crop}. Area: {col:costha.area_ha} hectares. Crop manager: {col:costha.manager}.

This season the field has used seed worth {col:costha.seed_cost}, fertiliser worth {col:costha.fert_cost}, crop protection worth {col:costha.prot_cost} and other inputs worth {col:costha.other_cost}. The total is {col:costha.total_cost}, or {col:costha.cost_ha} per hectare.

The budget set on {col:costha.budget_set} is {col:costha.budget_ha} per hectare, {col:costha.budget_total} for the field. The cost is {col:costha.vs_budget} against the budget and the budget check shows: {col:costha.state}.
If the check shows over budget, the crop manager reviews the next issues from the store and writes the reason in the season review.
Field: {col:irrsched.field}. Crop: {col:irrsched.crop}. System: {col:irrsched.system}. Area: {col:irrsched.area} hectares. Supervisor: {col:irrsched.supervisor}.

The field is watered from {col:irrsched.source}, which delivers {col:irrsched.flow} cubic metres per hour. Each turn applies {col:irrsched.depth_mm} mm, which is {col:irrsched.m3_turn} cubic metres and {col:irrsched.hours_turn} hours of pumping, every {col:irrsched.interval} days.

The last run was on {col:irrsched.last_run}. The next turn is on {col:irrsched.next_due}, in {col:irrsched.days_to} days. The turn check shows: {col:irrsched.state}. Water due this week: {col:irrsched.m3_week} cubic metres.
The supervisor writes the hours run and any fault in the irrigation log the same day. The lines are flushed on {col:irrsched.flush_date}.
Water use report for a source

The source delivers {col:water.flow_m3h} cubic metres per hour and serves {col:water.served_ha} hectares. The yearly quota is {col:water.quota_m3} cubic metres. This season we have used {col:water.used_m3} cubic metres, which is {col:water.share} of the quota. The quota check shows: {col:water.quota_state}.

The licence check shows: {col:water.licence_state}, with {col:water.licence_days} days to go. The pump service is due on {col:water.pump_service} and the service check shows: {col:water.service_state}. Pump energy cost this season: {col:water.energy_cost}.
This report goes to the water authority on request and stays with the licence papers.

{col:quotes.vendor} quoted {col:quotes.price} per unit with {col:quotes.transport} for transport, a landed price of {col:quotes.landed} and a total of {col:quotes.total}. The lead time is {col:quotes.lead_days} days and the quote is valid until {col:quotes.valid_until}.

The quote ranks number {col:quotes.rank}. The best landed price for this input is {col:quotes.best}. Choosing this quote instead of the best one costs {col:quotes.extra} more. The quote check shows: {col:quotes.state}.
We choose on the landed price and the cost of each kilogram of nutrient, then on the lead time and the record of the supplier.

The batch was received on {col:chem.received} and expires on {col:chem.expiry}, which is in {col:chem.days_to_expiry} days. The quantity in the store is {col:chem.qty} {col:chem.unit}, worth {col:chem.value}. The expiry check shows: {col:chem.state}.
The storekeeper is {col:chem.keeper}. Expired products are kept apart and labelled, and are returned to the supplier or handed to an approved collector. They are never used and never poured away.
This inventory is kept with the safety data sheets and is shown to the inspector on request.
Record: {col:apps.app_id}. Date of application: {col:apps.date}. Field: {col:apps.field}, {col:apps.area} hectares.

Product: {col:apps.item}. Method: {col:apps.method}. Rate: {col:apps.rate} kg per hectare, {col:apps.qty} kg in all. This supplied {col:apps.n_kg} kg of nitrogen, {col:apps.p_kg} kg of P2O5 and {col:apps.k_kg} kg of K2O, which is {col:apps.n_ha} kg of nitrogen per hectare.
The operator was {col:apps.operator}. The plan check shows: {col:apps.state}.
This record is kept for the number of years the law requires and is shown to the inspector together with the fertiliser plan and the soil tests.
Seasonal input budget for one input
The price now is {col:items.price} per {col:items.unit}, against {col:items.prev_price} last season, a change of {col:items.change}. The price check shows: {col:items.state}.

We bought {col:items.spend} of this input this season. We hold {col:items.stock_bal} {col:items.unit} in stock, worth {col:items.stock_value}. Each kilogram of nutrient costs {col:items.cost_nutrient}.
We use this page when we set the input budget for the next season and when we choose how much to buy early.

The label requires {col:limits.withhold} days between the last spray and the harvest, at most {col:limits.max_sprays} sprays and a dose of no more than {col:limits.max_dose} per hectare. People may re-enter after {col:limits.reentry} hours.

We have recorded {col:limits.sprays_used} sprays this season. The last spray was on {col:limits.last_use}, so the crop is safe to harvest from {col:limits.safe_from}. The harvest check shows: {col:limits.state}.
No crop is harvested before this date. The date is entered in the harvest plan and checked by the crop manager.

Open Start and type your farm name, the first day of the season and your own limits in the yellow cells: electricity price, days of cover, expiry and licence warnings, water quota warning and price tolerance.
List your inputs on Input Price List with unit, price now, price last season, supplier and the nitrogen, phosphate and potash share of each fertiliser. Add your suppliers on Supplier Performance.
Enter every invoice line on Input Purchases and every issue from the store on Input Use per Field. Enter each fertiliser spreading on Fertiliser Applications and manure on Manure and Compost.
Set the opening stock and reorder point of each input on Input Stock by Store and enter the count date and the number you counted. Balance, days of cover and the order quantity fill in.
List your fields on Input Cost per Hectare with the budget per hectare. Season cost and the budget check fill in from the issues and applications.
Type the kilograms of N, P2O5 and K2O per hectare for each field on Fertiliser Plan and read how much has already been applied.
Fill Crop Protection Programme, Withholding Periods and Chemical Store Register so that you know the first safe harvest day and which batches have expired.
Record price quotes on Supplier Quotes, orders and deliveries on Input Orders and monthly prices on Input Price History.
List every borehole, intake, canal turn and dam on Water Sources and Licences, and set each field on Irrigation Schedule with depth, days between turns and the water source.
Log every irrigation run on Irrigation Log, weekly pump hours and kilowatt hours on Pump Runs and Energy, and meter readings on Water Meter and Budget.
Use the 14 calculators for fertiliser, nutrient balance, blends, irrigation time, pump energy, crop water, drip flow, reorder point, quotes, budget, price rise, rain credit, manure and withholding.
Print 10 sheets and 10 letters, follow 10 checklists and tap a message link to open WhatsApp with the text ready.
Read Inputs and Water Dashboard and Charts every week: spend, stock, orders, nitrogen, water, pump cost, licences and expiry.

Withdrawal tracker for milk and meat
every treatment with a withholding period gets a release date for milk and for meat, the days left and a warning so nothing is sold too early
each scan result and the due date from the vet show births due in 30 days, overdue births and animals that need a recheck
Breeding records with return to heat
the due date and the expected return to heat come from the gestation days of the group, and every service is marked confirmed, returned to heat or calved
Growth and daily gain against target
each weighing is compared with the one before and with the target gain of the group, so slow animals and batches show up at once
planned, given, due soon and overdue vaccinations for every group, with the doses used and the coverage reached
Ration cost and dry matter per group
the feeds of each ration are priced from your purchases, giving cost per head per day, dry matter as a share of body weight and feed per kilogram of gain
Feed orders with days of feed covered
each order shows what it costs, how many days of feed it covers at the real use of the group and whether it is late
the day a paddock is free, the rest it needs and the stocking rate per hectare show whether it is grazed, resting or ready
floor area against the space each animal needs gives the capacity of every house and pen and warns before a house is overfull
Mortality log with rate and cause
every loss is recorded with its cause and value, and each group's yearly mortality rate is checked against the limit you accept
stock, reorder level, expiry date and withholding days of every medicine and vaccine with warnings for expired, expiring and low stock
Biosecurity gate log with waiting rule
each visitor is checked against the days since other livestock contact and disinfection, and is allowed, told to wait or flagged

Herds and flocks: head, feed cost, gain and health
One row for each group with house, keeper and standards; head now, livestock units, feed cost, daily gain, deaths and health counts fill in from the other sheets.
Feed cost per head per day
One row for each ear tag with breed, sex, birth date and status; group, species, age, last weight, treatments and withdrawal status fill in by themselves.
Births: calving, lambing, kidding and farrowing
One row for each birth with dam, sire and young born; group, species, interval since the dam last gave birth, the service date and the real gestation days fill in.
Breeding records with due date and return to heat
One row for each service or insemination; due date, expected return to heat, days to birth and the result of the service fill in from the dam, the group standards and the pregnancy checks.
One row for each pregnancy check with the result and the due date the vet gives; group, days to birth and whether the birth is near, overdue or done fill in.
Weights and growth with daily gain against target
One row for each weighing of an animal or a batch; the previous weighing, the daily gain and a check against the target gain of the group fill in.
Vaccination schedule per group with overdue warnings
One row for each planned vaccination; type the day it was given and the doses used; the next date, coverage and whether it is given, due soon or overdue fill in.
One row for each treatment with the animal, cause, medicine and dose; the withholding days, the last treatment day and whether the treatment is still running fill in.
Withdrawal tracker: milk and meat that may not be sold
One row for each treatment that has a withholding period; the milk and meat release dates, the days left and whether the animal is still under withdrawal fill in from the treatment and the medicine.
One row for each visit with the vet, group, purpose, findings and cost; the follow-up status and the keeper phone fill in.
Disease and mortality log with the cause of every loss
One row for each loss with group, number of animals, cause and value; house, share of the group and whether the loss is in the last 12 months fill in.
Feed rations per group with cost and dry matter
One row for each feed in a ration with the kilograms per head per day; price, cost per head, dry matter, kilograms and cost for the whole group fill in.
As fed, kg per head per day
Cost per kg if grown here
Feed purchases and deliveries with days of feed covered
One row for each feed order with supplier, quantity, price and dates; cost, the days of feed the order covers and whether it is ordered, delivered, late or overdue fill in.
Feed use per group: weekly totals of bought feed
One row for each group, feed and week with the kilograms fed; the feed per head per day and the cost fill in at the average price you paid.
Grazing rotation with rest days and stocking rate
One row for each grazing period of a paddock; the day the group leaves, the day the paddock is ready again, the stocking rate and whether the paddock is grazed, resting or ready fill in.
Housing and pens: space, capacity and stocking density
One row for each house or pen with its floor area, the space each animal needs and the head inside; capacity, space per head, share used and a warning when it is full fill in.
Animal movements: born, bought, sold, died and moved
One row for each movement with group, number of animals, who took or sent them and the value; the signed head, weight and price per head fill in, and the head of each group updates itself.
Culling list with reasons and expected value
One row for each animal chosen to leave the herd with the reason and the expected value; group, age, last weight and whether it is planned, near or done fill in.
Biosecurity visitors log with the waiting rule
One row for each visitor or vehicle with the farm visited before and the days since that contact; a rule shows whether the visitor may enter, must wait or was not disinfected.
Medicine stock with expiry dates and withholding periods
One row for each medicine or vaccine with the stock counted, reorder level, expiry date and withholding days; use in 12 months, stock value and a warning for expired, expiring or low stock fill in.
